desc:
A group of people must cross a narrow bridge at night. times[i] is the number of minutes person i needs to walk across. There is only one torch, so:

  • at most two people may be on the bridge at the same time;
  • a group on the bridge always walks at the pace of its slower member;
  • the torch must be carried back to the start by someone before the next group can cross.

Return the minimum total number of minutes in which everybody can reach the other side.

times = [1, 2, 5, 10]   -> 17
times = [3, 5]          -> 5
times = [4]             -> 4
hints: Small cases first: one person crosses alone, two cross together, three people can be done in a fixed way. What is the bottleneck for four or more?
Sort the times. The two slowest people should cross together at some point, because otherwise each of them costs a full slow trip alone.

While more than 3 people remain, move the two slowest across using the cheaper of two plans: (a) the fastest escorts the second fastest... i.e. t0 + 2*t1 + t[last], or (b) the fastest shuttles twice: 2*t0 + t[last-1] + t[last]. Then continue with two fewer people. Finish the last 1, 2 or 3 people directly.
editorial: Sort the times ascending. The two slowest people x = t[n-1] and y = t[n-2] must both cross, and the best is to send them together so that only the larger time x is paid. Two ways accomplish this and return the torch: (a) fastest and second fastest cross (cost t1), fastest returns (t0), the two slowest cross (x), second fastest returns (t1): total t0 + 2*t1 + x; (b) fastest escorts the slowest (x), returns (t0), escorts the second slowest (y), returns (t0): total 2*t0 + x + y.

After either plan, the two slowest are done and the torch is back with the rest, so the same problem remains with two fewer people. Take the cheaper plan each time (an exchange argument shows no other pattern is better). Base cases: 1 person: t0; 2 people: t1; 3 people: t0 + t1 + t2. Sorting dominates: O(n log n).
